slides.title: Acme should move upmarket to enterprise HR in 2026, funded by sunsetting SMB — adding an estimated $40M ARR over 24 months
slides.context: Acme has been a top-3 player in US mid-market HR software for five years. The board must now decide where to invest the 2026 growth budget to restart double-digit growth.
supporting_points: **Growth has stalled at 3%** for two years while three competitors have grown 25%+ by moving upmarket
**The enterprise segment is $4.2B** and growing 18% — three times our current addressable market
**Two of our top-30 customers** already use Acme above 500 employees and would expand within 12 months
**The product gap is six features**, deliverable in three quarters with current capacity
**The SMB tier costs $14M annually** to serve and is contribution-margin negative in 60% of accounts
decisions: Approve the move upmarket to enterprise HR as the 2026 growth priority
Approve the SMB tier sunset over 18 months, starting in Q2 2026
Release the budget for 3 enterprise sales hires in Q2 2026
slides.why_now: The 9-month feature lead holds only if the build starts in Q2 2026
slides.source: Strategy team analysis; Acme financials FY24
slides.name: the summary page

slides.title: Growth has stalled at 3% for two years while three competitors have grown 25%+
slides.framing_line: Based on Acme financials FY23–FY24 and competitor 10-K filings (n=3 peers)
bullets: Acme revenue grew 3% in FY23 and 3% in FY24 — flat against a market growing 11% annually
The three largest competitors each grew 25%+ over the same period, gaining 6pp of combined share
The gap concentrates in enterprise accounts, where Acme win rates trail the leaders by 18pp
slides.source: Acme financials FY23–FY24; competitor 10-K filings; team analysis

slides.title: The enterprise segment is $4.2B and growing 18% — three times our current addressable market
slides.framing_line: US HR software for companies with 500+ employees; market sizing from Gartner 2024
bullets: Enterprise HR software in the US is a $4.2B market, growing 18% a year
Acme's current mid-market addressable market is one third of that size
Two of our top-30 customers already use Acme above 500 employees and would expand within 12 months
slides.source: Gartner 2024; Acme customer data FY24; customer interviews, Feb 2026
slides.name: the market page

slides.title: Three of our five product lines fall in the low-growth, low-margin quadrant
slides.source: Acme product P&L FY24; market growth from Gartner 2024

slides.title: Of four growth paths, only enterprise expansion meets all three criteria

slides.title: The SMB tier costs $14M annually to serve and is contribution-margin negative in 60% of accounts
slides.framing_line: Fully loaded cost to serve by account, Acme financials FY24
bullets: Serving the SMB tier costs $14M a year across support, onboarding and billing
60% of SMB accounts are contribution-margin negative after cost to serve
Sunsetting the tier over 18 months frees the $14M that funds the enterprise build
slides.source: Acme financials FY24; cost-to-serve analysis, March 2026
slides.name: the SMB page

callout.label: What protects SMB revenue during the sunset
callout.text: An 18-month transition period and a partner referral program; the tier leaves the price list only in Q3–Q4 2026.

slides.title: Combined: enterprise expansion adds $40M ARR by end-2027; sunsetting SMB frees $14M to fund it
slides.placeholder_text: [ Waterfall chart: FY25 ARR → +Enterprise → +Existing expansion → −SMB churn → FY27 ARR ]
slides.caption: Net new ARR of +$26M, plus $14M annual cost savings from SMB sunset, for a total $40M EBITDA improvement.

slides.title: Implementation in three phases over 18 months, with the SMB sunset starting in Q2 2026
slides.framing_line: 18-month plan, Q2 2026 through H1 2027; owners per milestone in the appendix
slides.name: the roadmap page

slides.title: The board is asked for three decisions in April 2026 so that the build starts in Q2 2026
slides.framing_line: Each decision is paired with the safeguard that answers its main risk

decisions.decision: Approve the move upmarket to enterprise HR as the 2026 growth priority
decisions.detail: Six features in three quarters with current engineering capacity
decisions.safeguard: Go/no-go review after the first 5 enterprise wins

decisions.decision: Approve the SMB tier sunset over 18 months, starting in Q2 2026
decisions.detail: Frees the $14M a year that funds the enterprise build
decisions.safeguard: 18-month transition period and partner referral program

decisions.decision: Release the budget for 3 enterprise sales hires in Q2 2026
decisions.detail: Sales cycles of 6–9 months require hiring before the product is ready
decisions.safeguard: Existing top-30 accounts as anchor customers

slides.why_now: The 9-month feature lead over competitors holds only if the build starts in Q2 2026.

next_steps.task: Begin SMB sunset communication to customers and partners
Report the first 5 enterprise wins to the board

slides.source: Implementation plan, March 2026; risk review with executive team, March 2026
slides.name: the decisions page

slides.title: Key risks and mitigations span three categories: sales cycle, customer churn, and competitive response
bullets: Enterprise sales cycle (6–9 months): mitigated by using existing top-30 accounts as anchor customers
SMB churn during sunset: mitigated by 18-month transition period and partner referral program
Competitive response: mitigated by 9-month feature lead and existing customer relationships
slides.source: Risk review with executive team, March 2026
